$comment: Threat-class catalogue. Each entry names a class of exploit observed in the public
record and states, for this system, either the guard that refuses it or the reason it
is out of scope. Every claim here is CHECKED MECHANICALLY by
.github/scripts/assurance/threat_coverage.py: a guard symbol that no longer exists in
src/, or a test that no longer exists in test/, fails the build. A claim that cannot be
Guards are named by SYMBOL, never by line number. Line numbers are valid only against a
pinned revision and a stale anchor is a false claim.
Taxonomy sources: DASP Top 10; the SWC registry (frozen since 2020, retained for
cross-reference only); the exploit classes catalogued in the peer-reviewed systematisations
of DeFi incidents. Coverage of any single taxonomy is necessarily partial: the published
evaluations of automated detectors against real incidents report that most real losses fall
outside what one taxonomy enumerates. This file is therefore a floor on what we have
considered, not a ceiling on what exists.

classes.class: Reentrancy
classes.note: Every value-moving entry point is guarded; the callback surface authenticates its caller.

classes.class: Access control
classes.note: Four distinct roles; the control plane can be renounced permanently and what survives renunciation is enumerated and tested.

classes.class: Arithmetic over/underflow
classes.note: Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic throughout; every `unchecked` block carries a written bound argument, and the representability of the hard curves is tested at the boundary.

classes.class: Denial of service by unbounded iteration
classes.note: Route shape is bounded in every dimension: hops, legs per hop, legs per route, candidates, registry seats.

classes.class: Transaction-order dependence / sandwiching
classes.note: An output floor is enforced by the executor independently of the caller's own minimum, and the caller's minimum may only tighten it.

classes.class: Cross-function reentrancy through an external venue
Price-oracle manipulation
classes.note: There is no external price feed to manipulate: the reference quote is produced on chain, in the same frame as execution, from the venues actually traded. The floor is derived from that quote.

classes.class: Caller-supplied quantity substituted for a measured one
classes.note: Declared route figures are treated as coordinates to measure at, never as values to act on. The fee base is re-derived from the on-chain quote of the legs as executed.

classes.class: Fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens
classes.note: Every amount that matters is a measured balance delta, never an assumed transfer amount.

classes.class: Hostile venue admitted to the registry
classes.note: Venue admission is curator-only, one row per address, and the derivation origin is attested at admission and frozen once control is renounced.

classes.class: Admitted venue whose logic moves behind a proxy
classes.note: Re-admission after renunciation is refused when the runtime moved. Where a proxy can move its ANSWER without moving its code, the answer is pinned instead of the code.

classes.class: Venue row converted from a derived origin to an asked one after ossification
classes.note: A derived origin is a theorem the venue cannot influence; an asked one is whatever it answers. The codehash pin does not see the difference, because it is satisfied by code that never moved. The transition is refused once control is renounced; tightening in the other direction stays allowed.

classes.class: Published metric that reports the caller's declaration rather than the measured flow
classes.note: The registry is handed what each leg's venue took in, measured on the venue's side (Router legTook, fin2-relogio 2026-11-11), rather than the figure written in the route. Until then it was the hop's measured-over-declared spend ratio (hopScale).

classes.class: Preview that does not predict execution
classes.note: Parity between the published quote and the realised delivery is asserted in both fee regimes.

classes.class: Execution-grade quote that execution cannot honour as a minimum output
classes.note: previewPlanExact publishes the figure an integrator turns into userMinOut. Where the Router takes the protocol fee off an input, the venue prices the reduced input and its output is an integer step function of it, so a deduction off the gross output can sit a few wei above delivery. The exact pass funds the returned route as the Router will and publishes the lower figure; the stateful twin is invariant_exactOutIsAFloorTheRouterHonours.

classes.class: Deterministic pool derivation steered to an attacker address
Permissionless dust positions that truncate a bounded tick walk and steer the ranking
classes.note: Reported by Seavia Resources. One-wei positions on the ticks in a V4 pool's path cut the sixteen-stretch walk short. That walk stays the promise (a floor is safe); every ranking consumer (the probe rate, the held vote, the split gate, the route comparison) orders by the deep walk instead, which runs only while the rest of the input could still change the outcome, and a quote still truncated after the deep walk keeps the split rather than collapsing on a guess. The ceiling saturates at the larger of the rank and 2^128 - 1, never under the rank, so lo <= rank <= hi holds on every return and the Solver's unchecked hi - lo cannot wrap (B1, test_B1_TruncatedDeepWalkDoesNotRevertThePlan).

classes.class: Cheap activity pumps the ranking score and cuts the deepest venue before it is quoted
classes.note: Bounty #82 (root: dex-12). psi multiplies a swap count that costs one dust swap per unit by a depth weight that doubles per decade, so eight shallow pools pumped a few times each took every funnel seat. From 2026-10-13 the funnel measured every row it cut and always seated the deepest (_seatDeepest). Since 2026-10-27 no count cuts the funnel, so there is no seat to buy: psi only orders the rows, and the only rows dropped are dust, each measured by Core.registryDepth18Dec against the rest of its own pair and dropped under 25 ppm of it (the split gate's bar). The deepest row is never dust, nor is a rare token's pool alone on its pair. Since 2026-11-10 the measure is Core.hopMass18, the tokenOut the row can pay on this hop (the MAT-FUNNEL-MASS-TWO-TOKENS class): the registry's depth has no direction and, for a singleton book, no cap by what the book holds.

classes.class: Dust planted at the early cells of the V4 scan spends its count and hides a deep pool
classes.note: Report 3317 (Seavia Resources). The V4 derive scan stopped at eight proven pools (V4_CAP) and the cap was spent by whatever was probed first: one-wei hookless pools at the cells probed before the deep book (the native key's tiers, a code learned through claimV4, the canonical tiers) used up the eight, discovery never listed the deep pool and the Solver never quoted it. Since 2026-10-27 no count stops the scan: every stage runs on every scan, the registration's table bounds what it lists (discoverFor reserves 2 * fees.length + 10 slots per V4 row), and the dust reaches the Solver, whose funnel drops it against the pair's measured depth (_dropDust, SOK-FUNNEL-DUST-PSI).

classes.class: A pair registered honest forges its reserves afterwards and a recoverable donation buys the band
classes.note: Bounty #85 (Remember Me). reservesHeld was asked only at a pair's first swap; a synthetic pair registered honest, then forged getReserves, and the Solver's vote min(declared depth, tokenOut balance) collapsed to a balance a recoverable donation filled. 13M donated against three honest pools of 4M moved the depth-weighted median 6 % off fair and the victim was filled 548 bps under honest routing. Core.heldBy is now asked at every door that reads a pair's declaration: the quote dispatcher (V2 and Solidly arms quote a lie as dead), registryDepth18 (a lie has depth 0), the Router's in-frame quote (RouterE(8) before a wei moves) and the Hub's tick (a lying row is not refreshed). Alone it left a contract that HOLDS what it declares (a parked pair, a V3-shaped contract with a donation) voting, 588 and 522 bps; with the band vote of SOK-FORGED-RESERVES-BAND-VOTE in the same tree both measure 0 (test_ParkedHeldPairDoesNotVote, test_ConcentratedShapeWithADonationDoesNotVote).

classes.class: Malicious hook on a hooked venue
classes.note: hookAltersDeltas reads the hook's immutable address bits and refuses delta-taking hooks at three independent surfaces; hookRunsInSwap scopes the allow-list and the pin to hooks that run in a swap; hookPaused refuses revoked and code-moved hooks on every door; registry reads filter by isHookLive. Hooks with no swap bit are never entered by their own pool's swap and need neither list nor pin; one reached inside a swap through a nested PoolManager call made by an admitted hook is bounded by the manager's flash accounting - a delta it leaves unsettled reverts the whole unlock, measured against the canonical PoolManager on Base (test/fork/NestedHookSettlementFork.t.sol) - and by the same floors. For hooks that run in the swap, the list curates the AUTOMATIC door (registering a hooked pool admits and pins its hook) and the pin pauses a listed hook whose code moved on every door; the curator's revocation refuses on every door. A hook nobody listed is the caller's signed choice on the explicit door: what it does inside the swap is bounded by the in-frame promise, the attestation gate and userMinOut, which read no list, measured by the fuzzed campaign named as the test.

classes.class: Registry exhaustion by repeated admission
classes.note: One row per address; repeated admission of one venue updates its row instead of consuming a seat.

classes.class: Arbitrary external call or transfer-from sink
classes.note: The executor never takes a caller-supplied call target. Venue interaction is dispatched from a closed set of shapes selected by a registry-held kind.

classes.class: Signature replay on delegated approval
classes.note: Delegated approval is handled by the canonical permit contract; the system holds no signature scheme of its own.

classes.class: Governance capture
classes.rationale: There is no governance: no token vote, no timelock, no upgradeable proxy. The Hub and the Router each have one admin address. Their control powers (pausing, the role and configuration setters, removing a bridge, revoking a hook, and the Router's 48-hour rescue of tokens sent to it by mistake) end permanently when that contract's renounceControl is called. Venue admission is not renounceable: it outlives renunciation by design (addFactory, addBridge and allowHook for the Hub admin; addV4 and seedPool also for operators seated before renunciation). Admission only grows the registry; a listed venue is still validated at quote and execution and bounded by the per-leg floor and the caller's userMinOut. Nothing can move user funds.

classes.class: Malicious upgrade
classes.rationale: The contracts are immutable and non-upgradeable. There is no proxy and no implementation slot.

classes.class: Compromise of an external bridge or venue
classes.rationale: Third-party venues are composed, not controlled. Their failure is bounded here by the enforced output floor and by the caller's own minimum, but their internal security cannot be asserted by this system and is not claimed.

classes.class: Compromise of a user's private key
classes.rationale: Outside the trust boundary. Recorded because the published incident data attribute a large share of total losses to key compromise, and a threat catalogue that silently omits the largest class would overstate its own coverage.

classes.class: A route whose fields disagree with each other (the pool it names is not the pool its key executes, or its direction is not the direction of its tokens)
classes.note: RouterE(11) in _execV4Amt refuses a V4 leg whose named pool is not the pool its key derives to, or whose direction is not the direction of its tokens, before a token moves; the Quoter refuses to price a mismatched leg and holds the plan's own point. Reported by Karan Rathod (BPX-2026-009). A route that is consistent in every field is the caller's signed intent and is bounded, as every route is, by the in-frame promise, the attestation gate and userMinOut. Measured on both sides of the pool, per field, in the second hop of a two-hop route, in one leg of a split (test_SubstitutedHook_RouteNamesPoolA_IsRefused, test_SwappedTickSpacing_RouteNamesPoolA_IsRefused, test_Quoter_MismatchedLeg_IsNotPricedOnTheSubstitutedPool, test_V4_FlippedDirection_IsRefused, test_Quoter_FlippedDirection_IsNotPriced) and as the fuzzed accept-iff-consistent property named as the test.

classes.class: An interface that authors both the route and the caller's minimum (the caller signs a venue and a floor they did not choose)
classes.rationale: A route that is consistent in every field is the caller's signed intent: the venue named in the leg is the venue that executes. The absolute floors are the caller's own: userMinOut and, when the caller sets it, route.singleOutFloor (dropped on a route where a fee-on-transfer token was measured), both enforced as RouterE(5); every other floor is relative to the venue the route names. The Router does refuse some venues the caller chose (a V4 pool whose hook alters deltas, or whose in-swap hook is paused, reverts RouterE(9)), but it does not refuse a consistent venue for being a worse price than another, so the class sits outside the scope line in SECURITY.md (a defect is in scope where the measured floor or the caller's own minimum can be bypassed). test_ConsistentRoute_PoolB_Settles_ByDesign pins that boundary.
classes.note: Registered 2026-09-07. leg.pool always equals the executed pool id, so a wallet or a route verifier reading the calldata sees the venue that will execute.

classes.class: A dynamic-fee key under a non-zero protocol fee: the in-frame promise is zero
classes.rationale: Under a non-zero protocol fee the Router cannot price a dynamic-fee key in-frame, so effV4Fee fails closed and the leg carries no in-frame promise; the floor is then the caller's attestation (80 % of the Quoter's dry run) and userMinOut, and the registry refuses to claim such keys. The class is bounded by the caller's own signed floors rather than refused by a guard, which is why it is recorded as a scope decision. Refusing the leg outright is an owner decision recorded as open. test_DynamicFeeKey_UnderProtocolFee_PromisesZero pins the zero promise.
classes.note: Registered 2026-09-07 from the hook-admission review. An honest attestation from the Quoter's dry run keeps the gate; lowering it is the caller's signed intent.

classes.class: A dynamic-fee key whose hook runs beforeSwap returns a fee above slot0's lpFee: the quote prices slot0, the swap pays the override
classes.note: H12, oc-1018 m2 (Low), fixed 2026-10-19. The shared V4 quote producer fails a key with fee 0x800000 and BEFORE_SWAP_FLAG (1 << 7) closed, so swapBestExactIn and the Quoter's preview never promise it. The explicit doors keep the Router's in-frame promise v4LegOut, which still reads slot0; a caller-built leg there is bounded by the iron floor re-derived from realised output and by userMinOut.

classes.class: The preview's exact pass dry-runs a leg whose swap-running hook the Hub holds paused, which the Router refuses
classes.note: H13, oc-1018 m2 (hardening), fixed 2026-10-19. _simV4 asks the sieve's pause arm as Router._execV4Amt does (RouterE(9)) and falls back to the plan's claim, as for a delta hook. canExecute was already withheld by _hookRefusedIn.

classes.class: The preview's exact scalar returns the plan's claim as execution-grade for a leg the Router refuses (hook, key or native side)
classes.note: W3-F2, Luis_MZ (bug bounty, uid 3115), fixed 2026-10-21. A residue of H13: _simV4 refused the leg, _priceLeg fell back to the plan's claim, and previewPlanExact returned it while the Router fails closed with RouterE(9). _exact now asks _pack's own producer, _hookRefusedIn, and sets the scalar to zero at both exact doors; the route keeps its attestation. No funds at risk: the preview lied, the Router did not move.

classes.class: The preview's exact scalar and canExecute quote a route whose shape the Router refuses with RouterE(3): a leg that does not trade its hop's pair, a hookless leg after a hooked one, hops that do not chain
classes.note: revisao-total 2026-10-23, the V3 twin of BPX-2026-009. _hookRefusedIn asked only the V4 refusals (RouterE(9), (11), (8)); it now asks the RouterE(3) shape of Router._execute first, reading each pair leg's tokens as _legTokens does. No funds at risk: the Router fails closed; the preview promised a swap that reverts. Cold-quote gas +1 832 (QuoteFidelity, measured).

classes.class: The seed door writes a V4 row keyed to one pool whose depth is read at another pool's id (a declared hook the pool's id does not derive)
classes.note: revisao-total 2026-10-23. The tier is recovered on the hookless id, the V4Entry took the declared hook, and registryDepth18 measured the hooked id, a pool anyone can open and fill. Operator door (A3). The derived id must now be the pool (HubE(4)).

classes.class: A pair registered honest forges its reserves afterwards and a recoverable donation buys the band
classes.note: Bounty #85 (Remember Me). The Solver's band base is a depth-weighted median, and a synthetic pair registered honest by its own dust swap (tier 2) voted with min(forged depth, tokenOut balance), a balance a recoverable donation filled: 13M donated against three honest pools of 4M moved the median 6 % off fair and the victim was filled 548 bps under honest routing. Option (b): mass no curated row and no registered factory vouches for does not vote (it still quotes and executes). Alone it left a liar inside the band (93 bps) and a forged pair where nobody may vote (521 bps); with heldBy in the same tree both measure 0. Measured, pinned: a pair with no vouched mass and a contract that HOLDS what it declares still captures (588 bps, test_limit_NoVouchedMassAndAParkedHeldPairStillCaptures); a deep permissionless pool from an unregistered factory no longer sets the band against a shallow curated one (2451 bps, test_cost_ShallowCuratedPoolOutvotesADeepPermissionlessOne).

classes.class: An in-transaction route search whose cost a third party sets: permissionless dust positions multiply the ticks the solve walks until the transaction runs out of gas
classes.note: Registered 2026-10-12. swapBestExactIn hands the Solver a fixed SOLVE_GAS (12,000,000) and reverts RouterE(17) when the search needs more: fail-closed, no funds move, and swapExactIn (which takes a route computed off-chain) is unaffected. Nothing on the solve path reads gasleft(), and the fuzz tests testFuzz_SolveGasCapNeverDegradesThePlan_NearTheThreshold and _AnyBudget assert that a capped search returns the uncapped plan or reverts. Three layers bound the solve: 100,000 gas per venue quote (GAS_CAP), SOLVE_GAS per search, and the network's per-transaction cap (2^24 under EIP-7825; 32,000,000 on Arbitrum).

classes.class: Fragmented liquidity that pushes the off-chain route computation past the gas an RPC node allows for a call
classes.rationale: The cost of computing a plan grows with the number of initialized ticks a deep walk crosses, and anyone can mint one-wei positions; across two bridges the computation can exceed the per-transaction and per-call gas limits of the network or of an RPC node. The effect is liveness only: a caller who cannot compute a plan does not swap, and no funds are at risk, because every executed route is still checked against the caller's floors. A fixed cap on the off-chain computation would trade liveness on one route for a degraded plan, which the in-transaction cap (SOK-SOLVE-GAS) refuses by design. test_EntryB_OverBudgetRevertsCleanUnderTheTxCap asserts that the fragmented fixture's search costs more than SOLVE_GAS.
classes.note: Registered 2026-10-12. A caller can compute the plan on a node with a higher call gas limit, or quote a route that avoids the fragmented pools and pass it to swapExactIn.

classes.class: An EOA delegates to the Router (EIP-7702), so the Router code runs with address(this) == the EOA and every balance the swap measures and moves is the account's
classes.note: Defence in depth, added 2026-10-20 after H11 (the V1 drain shapes through a delegated account; 2.0.0's deltas already held them, test/Fix1019H11.t.sol). The deployment address is an immutable (SELF) and _execute, which every door reaches, refuses RouterE(18) anywhere else; the four doors are pinned in test/Fix1020SelfGuard.t.sol. A 7702 account calling swapExactIn at the Router's address is unaffected. Not covered: the callbacks, receive and fallback in a delegated frame (they do not reach _execute).

classes.class: A contract written by the attacker under a real pair, honest in every view (tokens, shape, reserves equal to live balances), refusing or short-paying at execution, takes a registry seat through one dust swap and is then planned for everyone on the pair
classes.note: rizki-3107 (Rizki Armando), 2026-10-20. Admission requires proof of origin: the swap door seats a pair-shaped or concentrated pool only if Hub.discoverFor (the derivation from the wired factories) lists it; the pool's own token0()/token1() check stays beside it, because a CREATE2 hit proves the deployer and salt, not the tokens (test_Create2HitOnOtherTokens_IsRefusedByThePairCheck). An unproven pool stays tradable on a caller-built route, at the caller's risk.

classes.class: Dust swaps through a Gate wrapper buy vitality: each swap counts once whatever its size, so a wrapper's use (and psi) is pumped for the price of gas
classes.note: gatevit-1021 (W5-C1 on the Gate's own count). A wrapper's swap ticks its vitalSlot only when the input is at least the venue pool's balance of the input token >> 16 and the output at least its balance of the output token >> 16 (each side in its own token, no cross-token comparison) and the output is non-zero; pinned on both sides and on an empty output side (test_GateVital_DustOutputNeverTicks, test_GateVital_NothingOutNeverTicks). Not covered: an LP who controls most of the venue's holdings can withdraw them inside one transaction and tick with a small swap; a singleton venue (one balance for every pool) makes the threshold large and fails closed.

classes.class: A Gate adapter declares a depth its venue pool does not hold, and the Gate's fitness ranks the wrapper by the word
classes.note: gatevit-1021. Gate.vitalOf caps the adapter's depth18 (read under GATE_QUOTE_GAS) by the shorter normalised holding of the venue pool, Core.shortSide18, the registry's own depth of a pair (registryDepth18's reserves arm), so one mass reads one depth on both doors at any price (coerencia-fix-1023: the cap was the larger holding, heldMass18, and a word on the long side outvoted the short side the registry reads; tests test_GateVital_CapIsTheShortSideHeld and test_Coherence_A_SameMassSameDepthOnBothDoors, mutants [631] and [758]; until MED, 2026-10-28, [758] was watched at the band by test_Coherence_A_DeeperAnchorHoldsAtAnyPrice, and since then a wrapper has no vote beside a stated fee, so the cap is watched where it is produced). A venue holding one side only now reads zero. Not covered: a singleton venue's balance is every pool's, so the cap there is loose and the word decides below it; an address the Gate did not create, or a cleared family, reads zero (test_GateVital_OnlyTheGatesOwnWrappers, test_GateVital_ClearedFamilyIsDead).

classes.class: A Gate adapter declares a depth that is not the venue's own word: a family formula, raw units across decimals (the side with fewer units read as the shallow one), the pool's balanceOf instead of its accounting, or a balance read while the pool is mid-operation
classes.note: adapter-depth-1021. ExtAdapterBase._depth18 is the one adapter producer: the shorter side of the balances the venue reports (Curve coins(i)/balances(i) by index, only when the lock probe passes; Balancer V2 getPoolTokens and V3 getPoolTokenInfo balancesRaw by list, matched to the calling wrapper's pair), normalised by Core.shortSide18, the formula of the registry's own depth of a pair and of the Gate's cap (coerencia-fix-1023; the larger side through Core.maxSide18 until then, mutant [756]). Mutants [671]-[678], [756]. Since gate-adapt-guardas-1023 a Balancer Vault inside one of its own operations declares no depth: V3 while `isUnlocked` (a swap writes the pool's balances before its debt is settled), V2 when VaultReentrancyLib's `manageUserBalance` probe answers BAL#400 (an exit sends tokens before it stores the pool's new balances). Tests test_BalV3_Depth18_ZeroWhileTheVaultIsUnlocked and test_BalV2_Depth18_ZeroInsideAVaultOperation, and both probes against the live Vaults on Base (test/fork/AdaptersFork.t.sol); mutants [750]-[753]. Not covered: the Gate caps by the Vault's holdings, which are every pool's.

classes.class: A last hop mixes a leg the frame prices with one it cannot (a Gate leg, a native leg with no in-frame quote), and the protocol floor's base shrinks to the priced leg's share, so the unpriced leg under-delivers inside the floor
classes.note: coerencia-fix-1023. Router._execute folds every leg with no in-frame quote into hopQuote with its attested figure, so finalHopQuote is the sum of each leg's best figure and only rises against the old base (the in-frame quote when any leg had one, else the attested figure). A hop with no in-frame quote at all reads its attested figure as before (NM-002, test_LiquidityGapOnLastHop_FloorFallsBackToAttested, mutant [130]); a blind leg attests nothing and still hands the anchor to expectedOut. Mutant [757]. Not covered: the per-leg floor (LEG_FLOOR_BPS) and Layer 1 remain the only check on a leg's delivery against its own attestation below the hop's floor.

classes.class: A Gate wrapper's use reaches the registry through a second door: the Router feeds an executed kind-9 leg to Hub.recordSwap, so two writers answer one quantity and the user pays a depth read and a Hub call for each
classes.note: gatedfresh-1022. Wrapper.swap is the one writer of a wrapper's use (vitalSlot, read by Gate.vitalOf). Router._recordHits skips a kind-9 leg as it skips a leg that did not run; Hub.recordSwap's KINDS_EXECUTABLE return stays as the fail-closed second check. Measured on the explicit door (release profile, warm wrapper): 325 657 to 315 391 gas per kind-9 swap; Router +25 B. Mutant [679].

classes.class: The automatic door seats a kind-9 row that is not a live wrapper of the Solver's own Gate: a stranger's contract, another Gate's wrapper, or a wrapper whose family was cleared
classes.note: gatedauto-1022 (owner, 2026-10-22: «gated na porta automática»). The Solver reads its candidates from its immutable gate's wrappersOf through Core.discoverWithGate, filters each entry by Core.gateWrapperLive and drops the Hub sweep's own kind-9 rows; the Router's dispatch keeps gateWrapperLive on the execution path at every door, the best door's self-call included (test_GateF2_BestDoor_SettlesKindExternal, test_GateF2_Solver_NeverPlansAWrapperWithoutItsGate). Mutants [516] [567] [683]-[687].

classes.class: Gate wrappers count toward the Solver's freshness quorum, so listed wrappers suppress the Hub sweep that would find a deeper venue
classes.note: gatedauto-1022. _registryFresh and MIN_FRESH_VENUES count curated Hub rows only; the Hub never holds a kind-9 row (seedPool refuses it, recordSwap skips it). Gated rows enter every merge, sweep or not. Mutant [688].

classes.class: An unbounded per-pair wrapper list makes every solve of the pair pay for each wrapper's adapter reads until the search runs out of SOLVE_GAS
classes.note: gatedauto-1022. Gate.create refuses a fifth wrapper per pair (GateE(16)). The list is grow-only: nothing removes an entry, so a cleared family's wrappers keep their slots for life (4 creations per pair, ever); a cleared entry costs a solve only its gateWrapperLive. Measured on swapBestExactIn, release profile, mock adapter: +110 393 gas per listed wrapper that loses; each adapter read is capped at GATE_QUOTE_GAS, and SOLVE_GAS exhaustion fails closed (RouterE(17)). Mutant [689].

classes.class: An admitted Gate adapter's view quote promises more than its venue delivers, so the automatic door plans the wrapper and the leg floor reverts the best door for the pair
classes.note: gatedauto-1022. Three guards and no permissionless proof. The floor: no funds move, the leg floor (LEG_FLOOR_BPS) and the hop check revert RouterE(5) and userMinOut holds the user. The band: since MED (2026-10-28) a wrapper, whose fee nobody knows, has no vote while a curated row of stated fee votes (Math._mutedVotes), and it is judged from above against that row's price, its rate read as its price (Math._inBand), so beside any curated pair a lie above the band is out (test_GatedAuto_ADeeperCuratedAnchorKeepsTheLieOutOfTheBand, mutant [980]; a 10k pair beside the wrapper's 1M venue in test_GatedAuto_OverquotingAdapterHoldsTheFloorUntilCleared) and a lie within it settles above the floor. Until MED the wrapper voted the mass its venue holds (Gate.vitalOf caps the adapter's depth word, mutant [691], watched where it is produced), and a lie above MEDIAN_FILTER_BPS (+-5 %) was out only under a deeper curated anchor. The clear: when the lying wrapper is the pair's only venue no stated fee votes, the base's fee is unknown and the band keeps every live row, so the pair's automatic door is down, explicit doors untouched, until a curated pair is seeded or the admin's Gate.clearAdapter takes the family out at every door (mutant [692]). Residual: after renounceControl a lying family keeps that door down for its pairs. A permissionless proof (a swap measuring the quote and retiring the wrapper) was built and dropped in review on 2026-10-22: permanent (CREATE2 cannot recreate the wrapper), triggerable by anyone for one material swap, and its false positives (fee-on-transfer, hooked venues, size-dependent divergence) are exactly the gated venues, so it handed a griefer a way to remove a legitimate venue for ever.

classes.class: An admitted Gate adapter that is itself malicious: it reverts in exec to deny the pair's best door, or quotes honestly to every view read and delivers less only in exec
classes.rationale: The adapter family is the admin's admission behind a 48-hour timelock with code pinned by hash; no on-chain check can tell a hostile adapter from an honest one at admission. The answer to a hostile family is Gate.clearAdapter, which stops it at once at every door, available until the admin renounces control; after renouncing a hostile family stays listed. Recorded 2026-10-22 (gatedauto-1022).

classes.class: A word of an external answer copied over the free memory pointer: a wrapper's psi, raised by anyone's material swaps, becomes the address the next encoder writes at, so every solve that ranks or prices the wrapper pays memory expansion quadratic in psi and the automatic door fails at SOLVE_GAS
classes.note: F1 of the gatedauto-1022 review. Core._gateVital, the one reader of Gate.vitalOf, copies only words 1-2 into scratch (returndatacopy(0x00, 0x20, 0x40) after returndatasize() >= 0x60). Before: the whole answer at 0x00, psi on 0x40; measured 33 988 102 gas for gateQuote with depth at psi 2^22 and RouterE(17) at the best door. The class is held by the Scratch memory guard in ci.yml (no assembly call or copy with a literal output below 0x80 may end past 0x40). Mutants [693]-[697].

classes.class: A score answered without its producer: a reader that skips the Gate's vitalOf for a wrapper the Gate would score above 0 drops that wrapper from the funnel (as one that reads the decay on another clock, or without vitality's floor, does to a live wrapper), and one that trusts a slot it could not read seats or cuts a pool on a word nobody wrote
classes.note: H1 (gas-h1-1026). Core.gatePsi reads the wrapper's vitalSlot through _askWord (capped at GAS_CAP) and answers 0 itself only for a slot READ at vitality 0 by Core.vitality at uint32(block.timestamp), the function and the timestamp Gate.vitalOf runs: empty (lastUpdateTs 0) or dead by decay (its last stamp 32 steps or more ago). Core.psi (v * 2^bucket) is then 0 at every depth bucket, the answer Gate.vitalOf gives after its depth read. Any other slot, and a read that fails (no code, a revert, a short answer), asks the Gate as before. Pinned against gatePsi at 59ecf3f and by hand over buckets 0..15: vitality 0, 1, 3, the floor, both sides of the 32-step horizon, slots no swap writes, any slot (fuzz); by vm.expectCall the call not made (an unused wrapper, a dead one) and made once (a used one, one at the floor a second before the horizon); the saving by gas probes from cold accounts (8 957 against 47 908 gas, mock adapter); a burning read costs GAS_CAP and under 20k more. Mutants [826]-[838].

classes.class: A view the planner trusts that catches its own callee's failure and answers a fallback: a fee() whose hook wraps a TWAP observe in try/catch answers the BASE fee when the observe runs out of gas, so the caller's gas limit, or an attacker growing the oracle ring, chooses the fee a plan prices
classes.note: aero-nova 2026-10-26 (the 2026 Aerodrome CL pools). Core.getV3Fee reads on its own budget CL_FEE_GAS, refuses to read on less than CL_FEE_FLOOR (empty revert), and does not take an answer that spent CL_FEE_TRUST or more: a failure swallowed at forwarding depth <= 5 has consumed at least that (EIP-150), and an honest read at the measured structural maximum (CL_FEE_COST, Base fork) stays below it. Mutants [839]-[844].

classes.class: A per-block dynamic fee written into a registry row as a static key: every later quote prices the pool at the fee of the block it was registered in
classes.note: aero-nova 2026-10-26. Hub._concRowFee is the one producer of a non-V4 row's fee at both doors: a V3 row carries the tier its derivation is keyed by only when the pool answers it, else 0, the live read; never the pool's fee() answer. The swap door writes 0 when starved, the operator's door reverts. Mutants [845]-[849].

classes.class: A probe read on caller-chosen gas: a pool that reverts early when starved (the 2026 Aerodrome pairs check gasleft() before their fee module) reads as one that has no answer, so the sender's gas limit re-labels a Solidly pair as V2 or writes a stable pair volatile
classes.note: aero-nova 2026-10-26. Core._askWord reverts empty (the house's out-of-gas signature) on less than ASK_GAS_FLOOR = GAS_CAP * 64 / 63 + 3 000, so every shape, stable and quote ask either gets the whole GAS_CAP or does not answer. Mutants [855]-[857].

classes.class: A replicated-curve fallback applied to a pair whose curve the reader cannot know: a pair without stable() (the 2026 Aerodrome V2) priced on the volatile curve under-asks a balanced stable pool and over-asks a skewed one
classes.note: aero-nova 2026-10-26. Core.answersStable gates the replicated curve in solidlyAskOut and legQuoteImpact: only a pair that answers stable() with an ABI bool has a curve; any other asks and quotes 0 when its own getAmountOut does not answer. Mutants [852]-[854].

classes.class: tokenOut that lands on the Router inside a leg's measurement window (the leg input's transfer hook, the V3 callback, the V4 settle, a pair paying more than asked) counted as the leg's output: it carries an over-attested leg past the per-leg floor and the attestation into the Hub (the Penpie shape: a balance delta credited with funds the measured action did not produce)
classes.note: DEX-11, 2026-10-27. _execScaled measures got as the Router's own tokenOut delta across the venue call; the window also spans the input transfer, the venue's code and its callback. The delta may not exceed declared, what the venue says it paid: V2/Solidly the outAmt the Router asks of the pair, V3/Algebra/Gate the out side swap returns, V4 the recv unlockCallback takes (returned through PoolManager.unlock). Else RouterE(20); a fee-on-transfer tokenOut delivers less and passes. Red at ae5f1ae: the V2 donation and the over-paying pair settled. V3, V4 and Gate donations: test_V3_ADonationInsideTheCallbackIsNotTheLegsOutput, test_V4_ADonationInsideTheSettleIsNotTheLegsOutput, test_Gate_ADonationInsideTheCallbackIsNotTheLegsOutput. Mutants DEX-11 G1, G1-V3, G1-V4, G1-Gate, V3 declared, V4 declared, lock. Limits: a V3 pool that reports more than it pays raises its own ceiling; a Gate wrapper declares the Router's delta across its adapter's exec, so a donation inside exec raises the declaration with it (a kind-9 leg writes nothing to the Hub: _recordHits skips it); on V2, V3 and V4 legs a tokenOut that credits more than it was sent is refused (fails closed).

classes.class: canExecute on a route with no hops, which Router._swap refuses with RouterE(3) before it moves a token
classes.note: opencode OC-06, 2026-10-27. _hookRefusedIn mirrored the RouterE(3) shape checks of Router._execute in a loop over the hops; on zero hops the loop never ran and it answered false, so previewRoute called a hand-built empty route with a positive totalOut executable. It now refuses n == 0 as Router._swap does. The exact doors already returned 0 on zero hops. No funds at risk: the Router fails closed; the preview promised a swap that reverts. Mutant [881].

classes.class: canExecute, or a positive exact scalar, on a hand-built route with a leg the Router's dispatch refuses: a kind with no engine (RouterE(8)) or a Gate wrapper whose family is not live (RouterE(19))
classes.note: Bug bounty lot 2026-11-10 (uids 4065, 3820, 3551 arms a and b). For a leg that is not a V4 leg _hookRefusedIn asked only whether the pool trades the hop's pair. Router._execScaled asks one more thing before it touches a pool: a kind-9 leg must be a live wrapper of the admitted Gate (BPC.gateWrapperLive, else RouterE(19)) and any other kind must have an engine (else RouterE(8)). A route with one such leg beside a delivering leg read canExecute true at previewRoute and a positive scalar at previewRouteExact, and reverted at the Router. The mirror now asks both, and does not refuse a zero-input leg, which the Router skips before the dispatch. The Solver never plans these legs; only the hand-built-route doors were reachable. No funds at risk: the Router fails closed. test/QuoterDispatchRefusalMirror.t.sol, mutants QS-1 to QS-5; since 2026-11-11 the engine-kind control seats a venue of each kind's own ABI and asks the Router to fill, and the dry-run doors are pinned to ask the mirror of the leg as the Router scales it (mutant QS-9). Not covered: a reserve pair whose out-reserve is zero beside a delivering leg (3551 arm c) is a state the view door cannot read without pricing; it still previews executable and reverts RouterE(8).

classes.class: a positive exact scalar (previewPlanExact, previewRouteExact) on a route with a concentrated leg (V3, Algebra) whose input token the pool receives short of what the Router pays it, a leg the Router refuses with RouterE(13)
classes.note: Bug bounty lot 2026-11-10 (uid 3984). Router._v3Callback pays a V3-family pool what it demands and measures the pool's balance delta; short is RouterE(13) (a taxed token is routed where the venue takes it, owner decision 2026-08-10). The exact doors priced such a leg by the pool's own swap, whose callback never pays, so no transfer was measured and the scalar promised the fill. The exact doors now run the leg backwards on the same pool: the pool pays the Quoter the input token before it calls back, the callback pays it to the pool and measures the pool's delta at the Router's seam, and the verdict travels in the revert; short sets the scalar to zero. A pool that pays nothing backwards leaves no measurement, and no measurement is not a tax. The encode doors (previewAndEncode, previewAndEncodeWithMinOut) dry-run too and ask the same probe after the floor: a refused route has canExecute false and empty bytes. The view door holds no token in a view frame and cannot measure a transfer; it does not ask. test/QuoterMeasuresTheV3InputTax.t.sol, mutants QS-10 to QS-13. Not covered: a tax on the leg's output token (uid 3988), which the Router measures at the recipient's balance after a second transfer of its own (RouterE(5)); a Gate wrapper leg (kind 9) is not probed.

classes.class: one batchQuote item whose solve runs out of gas leaves the items after it 1/64 of the batch (EIP-150), so they read zero for a book that is not theirs
classes.note: Bug bounty lot 2026-11-10 (uid 4009). batchQuote isolates a failing item with a try, but forwarded all the gas that was left to each solve. A permissionlessly fragmented V4 book (one-wei positions on the order's path) makes one solve exceed any budget; the healthy items after it were left 1/64 and read zero, or the batch itself ran out. Item i is now given gasleft() / (n - i): the share never shrinks down the batch, so an item that solves inside 1/n of the budget is quoted whatever the others do, and the last item is given all that is left. View door only; no funds move. Limits, stated: an honest item that needs more than its share and is not last now reads zero in a batch (ask it alone); an item that exhausts its gas last still leaves 1/64 for the answer, as before. test/BatchQuoteItemGasShare.t.sol, mutants QS-6 to QS-8.

classes.class: The encode doors return canExecute and the swap bytes for a deadline already behind the block, which Router._swap refuses with RouterE(4)
classes.note: opencode OC-03, 2026-10-27. previewAndEncode and previewAndEncodeWithMinOut copied the deadline into the bytes and never asked it. Both now share _encode, which asks block.timestamp > deadline as Router._swap does, withholds canExecute and returns empty bytes. The other doors hold no deadline. Sibling OC-05 (an amount above uint128, RouterE(3) in Router._checkedSwap) did not reproduce: in the V2 fixture Solver.findBestRoutePlan reverts (panic 0x11) before any preview is packed. No funds at risk. Mutant [882].

classes.class: The exact scalar of a route with the same pool twice in one hop prices every leg against the pool before the swap, while the Router runs the legs in turn: it promises more than delivery
classes.note: opencode OC-07, 2026-10-27. _exact priced each leg against the initial state; the second leg on the same pool meets the pool the first moved. Red at c516601: one V2 pair, an order of 0.1% of its reserves split in two legs, exactOut 5 bps over delivery, so a userMinOut taken from it is refused. The Solver merges a pool's legs and never plans it; previewRouteExact takes routes built off-chain. Fails closed: exactOut 0, as for a leg the Router refuses. Mutant [883].

classes.class: The exact scalar of a route built off-chain whose hop declares an amountIn other than its legs' sum: the exact door capped and split by the declared figure, the Router caps and splits by the legs' sum, so the scalar promised more than delivery
classes.note: Q773 (from hop 1) and T04 (hop 0), 2026-10-27. The Router never reads hop.amountIn: it caps what reaches a hop at the legs' committed sum and splits it by that sum, and at hop 0 it takes the protocol fee on min(order, sum) before the cap. _exact divided by the declared figure and, at hop 0, took the fee after the cap. Red at 3293d7f: a direct route into a bridge (where _fundedOut does not bound the scalar) whose hop 0 declared half its legs' sum was promised about twice the fill, and the Router refused the route the door returned (RouterE(5)); an order above the commitment was quoted the fee out of the committed legs (test_HopZeroFeeIsTakenBeforeTheCapAsTheRouterTakesIt). The Solver's own plans declare the legs' sum; previewRouteExact takes routes built off-chain. The Quoter now divides by the legs' sum at every hop and charges hop 0 as the Router does; the Router is unchanged.

classes.class: The quote prices a concentrated pool at the fee its registry row carries - the pool's fee() in the block it was registered - while the swap pays the pool's fee now
classes.note: DEX-17 (revisao-total K5; opencode dx/it0020), 2026-10-27. provenShape writes a CL pool's fee() into its row at registration, and quoteV3Fee returned that key first ('static key is truth'), so the Solver's leg and the preview priced the registration block's fee; the Router's floor asks the pool (cfgFee 0) and the pool charges its own. Measured on Base: Slipstream WETH/USDC sp=100 answers fee() 549 and 564 in consecutive blocks, 150..937 across 35 samples. Red at 2a384f0: registered at 150, charging 937, netOut 997050419999003087 > delivered 996265623599004655, so a userMinOut taken from the preview is refused; registered at 937, charging 150, the venue priced worse than it is (test_AFeeThatFellIsPromisedAsThePoolChargesIt). quoteV3Fee now asks fee() of a pool that is not Algebra-shaped first, one staticcall per CL quote; the key answers only for a pool whose fee() does not; Algebra keeps its order. No funds at risk: the floor was already live. Mutant [884].

classes.class: A Gate leg priced by quoteCall on a venue that prices by running the swap leaves the venue moved inside the eth_call, and the next pricing of the leg in the same preview meets a venue the Router will not
classes.note: 3330 (imnw313), 2026-10-27. _exact prices the plan as committed, then _fundedOut prices the route as the Router funds it; a Gate adapter with no view price is asked quoteCall both times, and the Balancer V3 Vault's quote runs the swap and returns without unwinding it. The funded pass met the venue the first pass had moved and exactOut fell under the floor it promises (PoC on a Base fork at block 52,900,000: 326 bps under delivery on a 0.01 ETH WETH->RATE route, 1,444 bps split over two legs). Red in a unit fixture (a constant-product venue whose query writes its reserves): exactOut 991241419527741341670 against a floor of 993218161492991487486, 19.9 bps under, and the venue's input reserve 1,997.2e18 above where the preview found it (both passes kept). Under-promise: the Router's floor holds and no funds move. The Quoter now asks quoteCall in a frame of its own that always reverts (dryQuoteCall), as _simConc and _simV4 unwind the swaps they run; the answer travels in the revert data, under GATE_QUOTE_GAS. The adapter is not changed, so any venue whose simulation writes is covered.

classes.class: The encode doors return canExecute and the swap bytes for a floor the venues, funded as the Router funds the route, cannot meet, which the Router refuses with RouterE(5)
classes.note: 3336 (Ash), 2026-10-27. The encode doors' canExecute was the plan preview's: _pack takes the protocol fee off the gross output, while the Router takes it off the input wherever no single hop into a bridge takes it off the output, and a venue's output is an integer step function of its input. On a deep V3 pool (1 bp, price 1, liquidity 1e30, a step of about 12.6 wei) 1013 in with a caller's floor of 1000 previewed netOut 1006 and encoded bytes the Router refused with RouterE(5) for a delivery of 997; red in the repo on that counterexample and in a fuzz over amounts and floors near the estimate. The iron floor is not at stake (965). _encode now asks _fundedOut, the funding pass the exact door has run since 1f1c4bf, and withholds canExecute and the bytes when it is under effectiveMinOut; the preview's figures are unchanged. The two encode doors are no longer view (selectors unchanged; call them by eth_call, like previewPlanExact). No funds at risk: the Router's floor held and the call reverted. Mutant [886].

classes.class: tokenOut that grows on the Router between toutStart and the final measurement outside a measured leg window (a rebase or a reflection fired by the hop-0 input's transfer, a fee push or a sweep) or inside a blind leg (no attestation, no in-frame quote, so no DEX-11 comparison) counted as the swap's output: the balance delta paid the growth of the stranded balance to the swapper
classes.note: 3310, 2026-10-27. The mirror of #45 (received capped at amountIn): _execute caps totalReceived, the balance delta against toutStart, at outCap: the declared figures _execScaled returns for the legs that make tokenOut, less the scaled input of the legs that spend it and the fee _chargeHopFee charges in it, each subtraction floored at zero (hop 0 of a cyclic route spends its input, measured against baseIn, before any leg made tokenOut). Red at 59ecf3f (4 of 8) and at c516601 after DEX-11 (3 of 8: a hop-0 restatement, a blind V3 leg, the loose A->C->B->C shape); green with the cap. A fee-on-transfer tokenOut measures less and passes; the excess stays with the rescue. Mutants [887]-[896] (3310 cap x3, made, sum, handed, handed floor, fee, fee floor, lift); the cap also hides a lost toutStart from an honest venue's swap, so TOUT-nobase now pairs with the fee-on-transfer swap and h11-1019 P2 with the loose shape (their old pairs pass mutated). Escapes: a venue that declares more than it pays raises the cap; with a fee-on-transfer tokenOut a restatement inside the transfer deficit still pays; tokenOut an intermediate hop leaves unspent (a V3/V4 partial fill) stays with the rescue; the hop scaling and the hop fee base of hop h>=1 were uncapped deltas until 4111 (BRIDGE-DELTA-RESTATEMENT). 2026-11-12: inside a blind leg's window the venue pays before its callback (the mock in that order since 2957178), so a restatement there also grows the venue's own payment; the swapper is paid the declaration in the units it was made and the growth stays with the rescue (test_ABlindLegIsPaidNoMoreThanItsVenueDeclared; measured: no later swap by a third party moves it).

classes.class: A concentrated V3-shaped leg priced as if its current liquidity went on for ever (the single-range figure): past the next initialized tick the book pays less, so the plan the Quoter calls executable publishes a floor the pool cannot pay and is refused at every door with RouterE(5), and the Router's in-frame figure is the same overstatement
classes.note: DEX-01 / 3331, 2026-10-27. One producer for the Solver's promise (_paysWhatItWalks, the plan's concentrated legs in route order on V3_PAY_READS = 12 reads for the whole route, on the rebuild's plan before its assembly return and on the plan built at the cap) and the Router's in-frame quote (legQuoteImpact, 12 reads per V3 leg): the pool's own book walked read by read, each read holding ASK_GAS_FLOOR first; a walk that finishes promises min(walk, single range), one that does not keeps the single-range band and never reverts on the pool's answers. A promise that falls comes off its hop, later hops are scaled, the route is assembled again; a build is ranked on the band, and since N1 the leader answers for what its books pay (V3-RANK-ON-THE-BAND). Red at 6a05394: 7 of 15 in test/V3PromiseIsWhatThePoolPays.t.sol (three with RouterE(5)), 15 of 15 with the fix; the read floor (a starved read never answered) in test/V3WalkNeverAnswersAStarvedRead.t.sol; mutants [991]-[1009]. Residual, by design: a book twelve reads cannot finish keeps the band and its route is still refused at its floor, no funds move; 3331's own two-hop Base route is such a book. Algebra (kind 6) stays on the band.

classes.class: A concentrated V3-shaped leg whose walk the reads (or sixteen stretches) cut answered the single-range figure f, the band: on a book that thins across the ticks the walk had already crossed, the promise and the Router's in-frame quote (protocolFloorOut) asked for more than the pool pays, and the route was refused at its floor (RouterE(5)) though the Quoter called it executable (4229: 8-10 ETH WETH->USDS)
classes.note: G3, 2026-11-13 (PR #123 guard review). A cut walk answers min(walked + outV3(rest, price reached, last liquidity read), f): every crossed tick counts, the rest stays a model on the last range read, and it never answers above f, so a promise only falls (same producer for Solver._paysWhatItWalks and Core.legQuoteImpact). No new read, no new constant: V3_PAY_READS stays 12. Tests in test/V3WalkCutPricesTheRest.t.sol: sparse (cut at a bitmap word), dense (cut at a crossing), thickening (the cap holds); mutants [g3-1]-[g3-4]. Residual: past the last read the model is the last range's, so a book thinning further is still over-promised up to f.

classes.class: A route ranked on a figure no venue pays: the leading build's concentrated leg ranked on its single-range band, or at the cap of a held book, over a venue that pays more, then promised what its book pays, so the plan settled what the walked book paid and the better venue was passed over
classes.note: N1 (DEX-01), 2026-10-27. The plan built at the cap is promised what its books pay (_paysWhatItWalks) before the rebuild is decided. A promise that fell hands its book back (fl), and the leader's topology is rebuilt in the same static self-call on WALK_GAS without the books that fell (_sitsOut), and once more with WALK when the leader is held; each build is ranked on what its books pay (_rebuilt) and leads only above the leader's rank less what its books did not pay. No margin is added: both sides are the Router's own in-frame figures, and a leg more is the split gate's question. Red at 027a26c: a 1e18/1e18 V2 pair beside a V3 book whose thick range ends one tick ahead of a 1e18 order settled 140427106070046065, and 384887155267496486 with the book held, where the pair alone settles 498547894994324565 (the order less the 28 bps fee); green at 498547894994324565 at both doors. Mutants [n1-1]-[n1-5]. Residuals: only the leader's topology is rebuilt, so a topology ranked below it on the band is not judged again; a split is allocated on the band, so the split the books would pay most for is not sought; when the leader is held and a promise fell the rebuild runs two builds on one WALK_GAS, and one that cannot finish them leaves the leader's plan, promised what its books pay.

classes.class: A venue behind a high fee that holds half the band's voting mass sets the base at its rate after fee, and the band drops the honest low-fee venue as too good, so the whole order goes to the worse venue
classes.note: MED, 2026-10-28. A probe's rate is out / probe after the venue's own fee, and the depth-weighted median of the rates landed on the worse venue's rate whenever it held half the voting mass or more; the fixed band of MEDIAN_FILTER_BPS (+-5 %) around it then dropped the 0.3 % venue once (1 - 0.003) / (1 - v) > 1.05. Red at b4138ee, 7 of 10 in test/MedianFeeCapture.t.sol: a 10 % venue of equal depth at the same price beside a 0.3 % one settled 897479999999192257 where the 0.3 % venue alone settles 994208399999008766, and a floor taken from the preview delivered that loss. The band now judges the PRICE, r * 1e6 / (1e6 - f), f the fee the probe itself was charged (Math._prices, Core.universalProbe), and its width is the no-arbitrage band of the two fees and the two probes' error bounds, no fixed bps (Math._inBand, THE BAND): row i stays iff p* (1 - f_i)(1 - f*)(1 - e_i)(1 - e*) <= p_i and p_i (1 - f_i)(1 - f*)^2 (1 - e_i)(1 - e*) <= p*. The base's fee counts twice above, so a base parked at the edge of rest cannot drop the honest venue: a drop from above needs an arbitrage G left open with 1 + G > 1 / (1 - f*), and the user's loss against the dropped venue is under 3G (derived in THE BAND, fuzzed in test/MedianBandMath.t.sol). A row of unknown fee (a Gate wrapper) has no vote while a stated row votes and is judged from above only; a base of unknown fee keeps every live row. The probe's error bound covers its output's rounding, the fee's floor on its input and its own impact (test/MedianProbeErrorBound.t.sol). Mutants [970]-[980]. Measured on the suite: 13 tests in 9 files drew an honest venue 0.9 to 5 % from another, inside the old band and outside this one, and now draw it inside (0.8 % or less, a note in each); the same-answer replays of 653b1dc and 8938b6a keep their books where the two bands agree, at the market or 20 % from it. Residuals: a venue cheaper than the rest by a gap the arbitrage has not closed falls out above once the gap passes the fees; a high-fee venue at the fair price now sits inside the band, and until each leg paid for its place (SPLIT-LEG-UNPAID-PLACE, the same day) the split weighed it by its depth and the gate kept only the best single venue: on mocks (two 0.3 % venues at price 1, a 10 % venue at the same price), at 0.3x the honest mass and an order a tenth of each honest depth the 10 % venue took 23.1 % of the order and the output fell 1.10 % (the old band dropped it), and at 1.02x the mass the gate collapsed the route to one honest venue, 0.49 % under the honest split (the old band: 9.68 % under); the error bound is not derived for a V4 walk across ticks, a Solidly stable curve, a concentrated range with L > 2^96 or a Gate's impact.

classes.class: A leg that does not pay for its place: a venue at the fair price behind a high fee takes its depth's share of a split, and the split pays less than the same split without it
classes.note: MED follow-up, 2026-10-28 (EVERY LEG PAYS FOR ITS PLACE). The split's weights are depths (Math._weights), and a split by depth is the best split only where every leg pays one price; since MED the band judges prices, so a venue behind a high fee at the fair price sits inside it. Red at 3975a50 in test/SplitLegPaysForItsPlace.t.sol: beside two 0.3 % venues of equal depth at price 1, a 10 % venue at the same price holding 0.3x their depth took 2307692307692307692 of an order of 10e18 (23.1 %) and the route paid 9366202448592925025 where the two honest venues pay 9470004286326618086 (-1.10 %); at 1.02x their depth the split with it lost to one honest venue alone and the gate settled there, 984393991900749526 against 989276854878431020 (-0.49 %); the fuzz found 9056856573573057851 against 9460983517672387461 (-4.27 %). Solver._placed now tries, in a split of three legs or more, the leg whose probe paid least (Solver._onTrial, a tie to the lower address), and only while another leg pays on average at least that probe's rate: an optimal split can leave a leg out only then (its rate at zero is at most the common marginal rate, which on a concave book is at most what a kept leg pays on average). The split without it, on the same weights with the seat where Math.seatOf puts it (Solver._leave), replaces it unless the split with it ranks MIN_SPLIT_IMPROVEMENT_PPM higher, the gate's price of a leg; no threshold of its own. Both cases now settle the honest split to the wei and the fuzz holds; a third venue at 0.3 % is never tried, and one at 5 % is tried and kept (+367 ppm). Mutants [981]-[987]. The same-answer replay of 8938b6a (test/MathBoundarySameAnswer.t.sol) draws its books where no trial runs, or where the leg tried pays (derived in its header): where a trial dropped a leg the reference kept, that leg had added 0.14 and 0.34 ppm gross for 90000 gas. What it leaves: legs leave one at a time from the depth split and the trials stop at the first leg that pays, so the split is not the optimum across fees (no split weighted by marginal price is computed); a split of two is the gate's question.

classes.class: A write without mass (a dust swap, a registration, a claim) moves a registry row's clock or a token's learned V4 tier: the swap count that psi multiplies, the stamp that decay, discovery freshness and the funnel read, the first sample of tau
classes.note: fix-1102, 2026-11-02 (reports 3536, 3537, 3545, 3552, 3554, 3555, 3575, 3645, 3652, 3663). Until then every Hub.recordSwap tick counted and the Hub stamped lastUpdateTs, dust included, and only tau read the anchor: dust pumped psi, kept a stale row fresh and a shallow seat warm, and the first interval was read whole. Core.tickSlot is now the one writer of the count, tau and the stamp, and moves them only on an anchored tick (Core.tickDepth18: the shorter side at least the depth >> MATERIAL_SHIFT) past the stamped second; a row is born with count 0 and no tick; the first interval moves tau an eighth of the way from the unmeasured step; inside a decay step the count falls on the chord. claimV4 writes v4CodeOf only after the row is admitted, the recordSwap doors only on an anchored tick, and a lighter witness never rewrites a heavier one. Each report is a case in test/fix1102/DustSealFamily.t.sol: the dust-touched row equals its clean twin.

classes.class: A token that answers true to the fee transfer and moves nothing, or less than the share: the share is neither with its payee nor booked to its slot
classes.note: Reports 3688 and 3995, fixed 2026-11-10. Router._push booked a share only when Core.tryTransfer read a refusal, and measured the balance only then; on a true answer it returned. A share that stayed on the Router after a true answer was in no ledger: the input sweep of the same swap handed it back to the payer, or it waited as an unowned balance. The push is measured on both branches and what did not leave the Router is booked to the slot (owed, TSLOT_KEPT). The answer is heard in one place: when the Router's balance rose inside the push (a positive restatement, test/PathologicalTokens.t.sol test_PositiveRebase_SurplusSweptToPayer_NotLeftInRouter) the delta measured the restatement, not the push, and a true answer is not booked. A true answer that moves nothing and credits the Router inside the same call is heard as a restatement and its share returns to the payer with the input sweep; a restatement smaller than the share inside the push is booked to the slot. test/FeePushBookedByTheDelta.t.sol: four answer shapes, each slot, input side and output side, the claim, a second swap in the same transaction, paid + owed equals the share by fuzz.

classes.class: A token that restates balances upward inside transferFrom, after crediting the Router: the payer's own growth is attributed to the pull and the balance held before it keeps its own
classes.note: Report 3948, 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11. The #45 clamp (a pull never counts more than was asked) exists because a balance the Router already held can be restated inside the pull. Router._received attributes the surplus of a pull (the delta above the ask) to the pull in the proportion of the ask to the ask plus the balance held before it, rounded down: a restatement after the credit grows both by one factor, so the pull's part is exactly the payer's growth and what stays is exactly the prior balance's growth, whether that balance is a donation or the wei the Router's own transfers leave on a share-accounted token. The route spends what it commits, the input sweep returns the rest, and the balance held before the pull is never spent (measured in the token's shares). test/PullOnAnEmptyRouterIsThePayersWhole.t.sol (nothing before the pull: the whole delta), test/PullSurplusIsSharedProRata.t.sol (one wei, a few wei, the Router's own share dust, a donation larger than the ask, both doors, fuzz over the prior balance, the ask and the factor).

classes.class: A floor attested on the gross input compared against a delivery made from the input net of the fee: where the fee rounds up to a whole unit out of a few, the Router refused the route its own Solver planned
classes.note: Report 4007, 2026-11-10, fixed 2026-11-11. Liveness, not custody: the swap reverted with RouterE(5) and nothing moved. The Solver sizes singleOutFloor on the input the Router executes with: it reads the fee calendar over the hops it assembled with the rule of Core.feeCalendar (the first hop whose input is a bridge, every hop when there is none, no hop when the route is one hop into a bridge) and scales the gross output by each charging hop's (base - fee) / base, rounded down, before the floor rounds up; the Router compares the attested floor literally, unchanged, and a route whose fee comes off the output is attested on the pre-fee output the Router compares. test/AttestedFloorIsSizedOnTheNetInput.t.sol: best door, classic door and the Quoter's exact preview, every whole amount 2..40 of a 0-decimal token and fuzz to 5000, the bridge hop, the output fee, the pin of the attested floor to the rate the Router enforces; test/FloorParitySolverRouter.t.sol reads the two-hop rate in the net frame. The exact preview, 2026-11-11 (the verifier's regression on the fix): Quoter._exact on two hops or more takes the fee out of carry at the charging hop, so its exact output is net already; it rescales the attested floor by the plan output in the same frame, Core.netOfInputFees (the one producer the Solver uses) on two hops or more, the gross totalOut on one hop, where the walk takes no fee. test/ExactPreviewFloorIsTheAttestedRateOnTheNetOutput.t.sol: the previewed floor rate is the attested rate, two hops through previewRouteExact and previewPlanExact and across amounts, one hop into a bridge, one hop with the fee on the input; mutants fin2-router-7 and fin2-router-8.

classes.class: A caller-declared amount answers the registry's materiality question: a leg's attested output, which the per-leg floor accepts up to 25% above the fill, anchors a pool's clock (swap count, tau, stamp) for a fill below the bar, and is published as the pool's volume
classes.note: fin-1111, 2026-11-10 (reports 3958, 4028). The family-A seal (REG-DUST-CLOCK) made the clock move only on a material trade, and Router._recordHits answered 'material?' with mulDiv(leg.expectedOut, hopScale, 1e18): calldata. A fill just under depth >> MATERIAL_SHIFT attested 24% above itself anchored the row, and counted. The Router now hands Core.tickDepth18 and Hub.recordSwap the leg's measured delivery (legOut, the Router's balance delta that _execScaled reads and bounds by the venue's declared payment, DEX-11), in both directions: an under-attested material fill anchors. Pinned from balances, never from Core: test/ClockAnchorMeasuredDelivery.t.sol (over- and under-attested, the boundary to one wei of input, taxed input, taxed output, two legs, two hops, fuzz); mutants [fin1111-relogio-1]-[fin1111-relogio-6]. The INPUT side followed on 2026-11-11 (fin2-1111): it was the leg's declared input rescaled by the hop's measured ratio, the Router's send, so a transfer tax taken between the Router and a pair whose short side is the input token left the pair under the bar while the send cleared it, and the row anchored. Router._recordHits now reads legTook, the input the venue's side measured (a pair's balance over its synced reserve in _execPairAmt; the input _v3Callback paid and saw land in the pool, never the in-side the pool returns, and zero when no callback ran; the amount the V4 unlock callback owed and settled). Pinned from the pair's balances: the same test file (receipt below the bar with the send above it, receipt over the bar with Volume.amtIn equal to the receipt, the boundary to one wei of input, two legs, two hops, fuzz over size x tax); the concentrated channels in test/ClockAnchorConcentratedTook.t.sol (a V3 pool that asks for half and returns the whole order, a claim above the budget, a pool that never called back, fuzz over demand x claim; a V4 position that runs out of liquidity); mutants [fin2-relogio-1]-[fin2-relogio-9]

classes.class: the bridge token of hop h>=1 restated DOWN by a rebase the hop-0 delivery fires, over a balance the Router held before the swap (F): a route that spends the fair share k*D instead of the measured delta bal - F, or the pro-rata share of a declared input, reaches F (the drain R3 / BP-15 closes); the caller sizes the declared hop-1 input to the stranded balance
classes.note: Guard: realIn = bal - foreignBase in _hopScaleImpactAndQuote (I4: the measurement wins), per-leg coverage floor, hop budget. 4111 (whitelistsol), 2026-11-11. The Router sees (F, bal, L) and nothing else of the bridge: a uniform restatement k fired by the delivery (bal = k*(F+D)) and a short delivery with F intact (bal = F + D - c, c = (1-k)*(F+D)) are one observation, and the instruments that would tell them apart (sharesOf, totalSupply) belong to the token that fired the restatement. So the window keeps the measured delta: hop h>=1 spends bal - F, the Router keeps F in the units it measures, and the restatement's cut (1-k)*F lands where a short delivery lands, on the swapper inside the floor they signed (SOK-FOT), refused past it (RouterE(5)). Green at e01b503 with no change in src; mutants [bridge-1112 a] (raw balance) and [bridge-1112 b] (pro-rata bal*L/(L+F): L = 1e30 spends all of F) each die by name, under test/Fix1112BridgeRestatementWindow.t.sol and test/HardeningR3_HopForeignBalance.t.sol. World R needs the hop-1 pair to hold B above its stale reserves (Core.heldBy refuses the leg otherwise, RouterE(8)). Residual, by design: inside the floor the swapper carries (1-k)*F in display and the Router holds F/k shares of the bridge; a positive restatement over F is OUT-DELTA-RESTATEMENT's side.

classes.class: a bridge (hop h>=1's input) that grows on the Router outside a measured leg window - a rebase or a reflection fired by a fee push: hop 0's through a hooked input, hop h's in the bridge itself - counted as hop h's input: the raw delta bal - bridgeBase[h-1] charged the hop fee on the stranded balance's growth and spent it, so the stranded holder's gain rode out to the swapper as declared output (the escape OUT-DELTA-RESTATEMENT published)
classes.note: 4111, 2026-11-11 (bug bounty). #45's clamp and 3310's cap, applied to a bridge: _owned gives both _chargeHopFee (the fee base of hop h>=1) and _hopScaleImpactAndQuote (realIn) the balance past its baseline and no more than the previous hop's hopGot, which _execute carries in amountIn at the end of every hop (no new stack slot); the scale writes what the balance holds past realIn back into bridgeBase[h-1], so the sweep leaves it with the rescue instead of paying it to the payer. Red at e01b503 (2 of 3: the hop-0 and hop-1 fee-push restatements paid 90.5 and 107.4 of the control's 49.6; the honest two-hop swap is the control); green with the cap, 3310's eight tests green beside it. Mutants [1090]-[1094] (4111 cap, fee base, scale, baseline, carry). Behaviour change for the owner: the swap's OWN restatement gain on a bridge (a positive rebase of the swap's delivery, fired mid-swap) now stays with the rescue as 3310 already does for tokenOut; a later hop whose fee eats its whole input of 1 wei reverts RouterE(8) where it used to proceed with nothing. Escapes: a restatement INSIDE a Gate leg's window is declared at the recipient's delta (Gate.swap), so a Gate hop 0 whose bridge restates on delivery passes DEX-11 and this cap alike (follow-up in the Gate, not closable in the Router); a NEGATIVE restatement of the bridge on the Router is retained, not drained (hop h spends the post-restatement delta, the stranded holder keeps the pre-restatement baseline), and the same clamp cannot tell it from a fee-on-transfer bridge.

classes.class: A singleton book holding none of the bought token is weighed by its virtual depth and drops the honest rows of its pair as dust before they are quoted
classes.note: MAT-01, audit 2026-11-06. Solver._dropDust weighed every row by Core.registryDepth18Dec and dropped row j when d_j * 1e6 < 25 ppm * (D - d_j). That depth has no direction, and for a singleton book it was the virtual depth with no cap by what the book holds: a one-tick V4 position at an absurd price, claimed through Hub.claimV4 with no privilege, took D and dropped the honest pair (1,000 WETH + 3,000,000 USDC). Red at e2c52e0: test_honestVenueDroppedByV4VirtualDust (now test_MAT01_AOneTickSingletonBookDoesNotDropTheHonestVenue), and in test/HopMassIsTokenOutHeld.t.sol a book holding only the sold token dropped the honest pair at four decimal pairs and one holding none of the bought token left the pair with no plan (SolverE(5)). Since 2026-11-10 a row's mass is the tokenOut it can pay (Core.hopMass18: a pair's held reserve of tokenOut, a concentrated pool's virtual reserve of tokenOut capped by its balance, a singleton book's virtual reserve of tokenOut), and what a singleton book adds to the other rows' D is capped by the tokenOut its sixteen stretches hold (Solver._heldBooks), read only when some row's fate depends on it. The rule and its 25 ppm are as they were. Not covered: a Gate wrapper is not read by the funnel and keeps its seat as before; a book that holds the majority of a pair's tokenOut takes the band's base (the 50 % breakdown point of a capital-weighted vote, see HOP-ONE-CUT-PER-BRIDGE-UNIT-GAP).

classes.class: A book holding the honest short side's count of the cheap token takes the band's base, and the order is planned and paid at the book's price
classes.note: MAT-02, audit 2026-11-06. Math._depthWeightedMedian walks the live rows by price to half of the summed votes and its premise is that the votes count one token. They counted two: a pair voted its short side (away from price 1, the count of the dear token) and a concentrated row was then capped by the tokenOut it holds (PROV-01). Red at e2c52e0 in test/Mat02BandVoteIsOneUnit.t.sol, 4 of 7: beside an honest pair of 1,000 A + 3,000,000 B, a V3 book at 1 B per A holding 1,000 B (1/3,000 of the honest short side's value) took the base, the band dropped the honest pool, and a swap whose minOut came from the preview settled 994208400000000000 where the honest pair pays 2949866166278610009188; restating B in a unit 1,000 times bigger changed the plan. Since 2026-11-10 every row votes the tokenOut it can pay: the sixth return of Core._quoteArms (a pair's reserve of tokenOut; Core.outSide18 for a concentrated pool or a singleton book), handed to the vote by Core.universalProbe and capped afterwards as before. The plan no longer depends on the unit of account (test_MAT02_RestatingTheOutputTokenInABiggerUnitLeavesThePlanAsItWas and its fuzz). Not covered: a Gate wrapper votes the Gate's word (depthWad); Math._weights reads a singleton book's mass without the walk's cap; the probe's error bound still reads the short side.

classes.class: With two hops and no three-hop rescue, one cheap singleton book per bridge drops the honest rows of each bridge pair and takes, or stops, the whole route
classes.note: HD-01, audit 2026-11-06 (hops2). The funnel's dust rule is asked once per bridge pair; a book measured by its virtual depth (MAT-01) cut the honest row of every bridge at the cost of a few units of capital each, and with MAX_HOPS 2 no longer route is left to rescue the order. Red at e2c52e0: test_HD01_OneCheapCutPerBridgeAcrossAUnitGapDoesNotTakeTheVictimsInput settled 99729878138123597 where the honest route pays 289392651744148172858586, and test_HD01_Liveness_OneQuietCutPerBridgeLeavesThePairRoutable found no plan at all. Blocked by the unit: a book adds to the other rows' D only the tokenOut it holds (Core.hopMass18, Solver._heldBooks). With a unit gap the red book held 0.13 % of the bought token the honest row holds; it now adds that and no more. What is left is a designed limit of the band, not of the funnel, pinned by test_limit_HD01_ABookHoldingMostOfTheBoughtTokenOnEachThinSideTakesTheRoute: a book that really holds more of the bought token than the honest rows of its pair is the pair's majority and takes the band's base (the 50 % breakdown point, test/BandBaseBreakdownPoint.t.sol), and with one bridge per route the majority is cheapest on the thin side of each bridge. MAX_HOPS, TOPOLOGIES and the 25 ppm are the owner's numbers and are as they were.

classes.class: A thin book far from the market reads a narrow error bound at the probe, becomes the band's base and keeps itself alone for an order it fills at a large impact
classes.note: ROUTEQ, 2026-11-13. Core.universalProbe formed a row's error bound with its impact term at the probe (1% of the order) while Math._inBand decides the whole order with it. On Base at block 49800000 (run 43410379085) USDC->DAI 10k went whole into one Pancake V3 venue 1631 ticks off the market, 47% impact, 6550 DAI out. Since 2026-11-13 the impact term is taken at orderIn, the hop's amountIn passed by the Solver (m = min(a, o) at the order, rounded up; an orderIn under the probe reads as the probe; a rank times the order past 2^256 saturates to m = a). Held by test/RouteQualityOrderSizeError.t.sol (unit matrix, floor, +-1 wei, saturation, fuzz, the Solver at 1 and 2 hops) and the fork assertion in test/fork/RouteQualityProbe.t.sol; mutants ROUTEQ in .github/scripts/mutants.py.

classes.class: A replicated Solidly stable curve whose Newton exit leaves k below the pre-trade invariant: the quote promises more output than the pair pays, and the route is refused at its floor or settles short
classes.note: 124-L2, 2026-11-14. Core._solY landed the converged exit on the safe side (K_post >= K_pre) with one +1 wei bump, which assumed _solK increasing in y; it is only non-decreasing: its floor(x*y/WAD) factor moves in steps of WAD/x wei, so with the input side below one normalised unit a single bump can stay on the K-deficient step (two climbs were needed in 1,167 of 26,251 sampled exits over the full domain, never three). Since 2026-11-14 the exit climbs one wei at a time while K-deficient, at most two, and fails closed past that (y0, out = 0). Held by test/SolidlyNewtonLandsOnTheSafeSide.t.sol (the thin-side unit case and its fuzz, the exact-arithmetic fuzz, the swamping input); mutants 124-L2 Core:1863 and Core:1863-fix in .github/scripts/mutants.py.
